blocks.orig: For 5 times in a row now, Tanzania is the winner of Best Safari Country in Africa. Over 2,500 safari travelers and experts participated in this large survey conducted by SafariBookings.com. The panel also included 22 renowned guidebook authors from e.g. Rough Guides and Lonely Planet. Tanzania came out as the clear winner. Also, Zanzibar, a popular beach extension after a safari, was very popular.
blocks.html: Five times in a row now, Tanzania has been voted Best Safari Country in Africa. SafariBookings.com ran this extensive survey, in which more than 2,500 safari travellers and experts took part. Among the panel were 22 well-known guidebook writers, for instance from Rough Guides and Lonely Planet. The result was a clear win for Tanzania. Zanzibar, a favourite beach add-on after a safari, also scored very well.

blocks.orig: Why is Tanzania the best safari country?
blocks.html: What makes Tanzania the best safari country?

blocks.orig:
Africa’s natural wonders
North Tanzania is home to three of Africa’s Seven Natural Wonders. Firstly Africa’s highest mountain Kilimanjaro, secondly the world’s largest overland migration named the great wildebeest migration and finally the Ngorongoro Crater which shelters have the highest concentration of wildlife.
blocks.html:
Natural wonders of Africa
Three of the Seven Natural Wonders of Africa lie in northern Tanzania. The first is Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain on the continent; the second is the great wildebeest migration, the largest overland migration on earth; and the third is the Ngorongoro Crater, which holds the highest concentration of wildlife.

blocks.orig:
Pure nature
Tanzania is one of the few countries where you can still experience an authentic safari. The national parks and game reserves cover almost 35% of the country’s territory. A huge territory with endless plains, dust roads and no fences. Pure nature with a stunning variety of landscapes, from savannah, lakes, and craters to valleys, forests, mountains and tropical beaches.
blocks.html:
Unspoilt nature
In Tanzania you can still enjoy a genuine safari, something few countries can offer today. Almost 35% of the country’s land is covered by national parks and game reserves. That is a vast area of open plains and dirt tracks without fences. The scenery is pure and remarkably varied: savannah, lakes and craters, but also valleys, forests, mountains and tropical beaches.

blocks.orig:
Interesting cultures
Tanzania is a beautiful mix of cultures. More than 120 ethnic groups live together peacefully, from Maasai Warriors to the Hadzabe Bushmen. Each of these groups have different religions, rituals, customs, art, music, and dance. You can learn about their cultures first hand by visiting tribes and local villages on exciting cultural tours.
blocks.html:
Fascinating cultures
The country brings together a rich mix of cultures. Over 120 ethnic groups, from the Maasai warriors to the Hadzabe bushmen, live side by side in peace. Every group has its own religion, rituals, customs, art, music and dance. On cultural tours to tribes and local villages, you get to learn about these ways of life first hand.

blocks.orig:
Safe and friendly
Tanzania is known as one of Africa’s safest countries due to the country’s political stability and the fact that Muslims, Christians and 120 different tribes live together peacefully. The Tanzanian people are very welcoming, friendly, and always willing to help.
blocks.html:
Safe and welcoming
Thanks to its political stability, and because Muslims, Christians and 120 different tribes share the country peacefully, Tanzania is regarded as one of the safest countries in Africa. Tanzanians are warm, friendly people who are always ready to lend a hand.
